text:
Maria J: Quick capacity pulsecheck — our hosted API forecast for next quarter shows a recurring weekday evening spike in us-west1 that likely exceeds our reserved GPU hours by ~16%. attaching a small snapshot below. we should decide whether to adjust commits, enable burst capacity, or optimize workload first.

infra-bot: :warning: Capacity drift detected — reserved utilization (us-west1) = 116% of committed baseline for peak windows (3d rolling).

Ajay P: Can you paste the numbers? is that 16% of peak GPU-hour demand or overall hours?

Maria J: good call. short table:
```
window,peak_gpu_hours_needed,reserved_gpu_hours,delta
weekday-peak,480,415,+65
weekend-peak,260,300,-40
monthly-total,8400,8200,+200
```
so it's concentrated in weekday evenings — the monthly delta isn't huge but the SLA risk is real during peaks.

Kevin L: also flagging billing: finance saw an increase in on-demand line items last month for us-west1. looks like some burst usage was billed at on-demand rates instead of drawing down reserved credits. @finance-bot any detail?

finance-bot: Last invoice (month 2026-02) shows on-demand GPU hours in us-west1 = 720, expected reserved-covered = 600. Possible mapping issue between commitment SKUs and project tags; finance will open a ticket with cloud billing.

Elaine R: Two parallel things: short-term mitigate risk (burst + throttles), medium term (negotiate commit swap or uplift), long-term (batching + caching improvement). I'd prefer to avoid immediately increasing commit unless forecast shows sustained growth.

Samir N: I can run a sensitivity sim. Maria, can you share the hourly qps trace and model memory footprint? I'll run +10% demand / -5% quantization scenarios and post expected GPU-hours.

Maria J: sharing link to traces in thread (private gist). baseline assumptions: 32-token avg response, model = rdx-13b-qa, kv-cache makes peak sequences ~1024 tokens.

Ajay P: For short-term, can we route a portion of peak traffic to eu-west mirror (lower load) and pay cross-region latency penalty? How sensitive are customers to +80ms?

Kevin L: Some paying enterprise customers in that cohort have SLOs that won't tolerate >50ms added. We can use region routing for non-enterprise buckets though.

Elaine R: Proposed immediate actions: 1) enable burst pool for up to 80 GPU-hours across us-central/us-west (owner: @Samir, ETA: 24h) 2) finance & infra to reconcile billing mappings (owner: @Kevin, ETA: 48h) 3) run sim and produce commit-recommendation matrix (owner: @Samir + @Maria, ETA: 72h) 4) quick throttling rule for non-SLA customers during 6–10pm PST (owner: @Ajay, ETA: 24h).

Samir N: I'll kick off sim now. initial estimate: with +10% demand, weekday-peak delta goes from +65 -> ~+100 GPU-hours. will confirm.

Maria J: noted. Also let's add a follow-up to talk to cloud account rep about temporary swapping unused reserved SKUs from other regions — if finance-bot confirms mapping problem, that might release credits.

Kevin L: I'll open the billing ticket and tag account rep. filing now.

infra-bot: :white_check_mark: Runbook action created: "capacity-pulsecheck-us-west1" — owners: Samir N, Kevin L, Ajay P; due 72h.

Maria J: thank you. if anyone sees sudden spike alerts, please page eng-oncall and ping this thread. :thumbsup:

Ajay P: ack.

Kevin L: ack.

Elaine R: ack.

Samir N: starting sims, will post results here.
